subject: Post-call: Aurora Health — Data use & training exclusions
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Aurora Health — Data use & training exclusions

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have everything captured and actionable. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Call summary (key points)
- Aurora does NOT want customer content or identifiable logs used to train Redwood models or any downstream model-improvement pipelines.
- Aurora requires audit logs for admin actions and request tracing; retention target: 90 days (Aurora to confirm final number).
- Data residency: production inference for Aurora must remain in us-east-1 for PHI/sensitive workloads; backups/archives also prefer US-only storage.
- Logging controls: should be configurable per-route (redact fields, suppress full transcripts, toggle request-body logging).
- Compliance artifacts requested: SOC 2 summary, DPA with explicit training exclusion, and an implementation timeline for opt-out enforcement.

Attachments I’ve included: redwood_security_summary.pdf (SOC2 summary, high-level), aurora_data-retention-FAQ.docx (template for retention options).

Concrete next steps
1) Elena: confirm the retention window (90 days vs 180 days) and whether the residency requirement applies to backups/analytics.
2) Redwood (me + Monica): prepare a DPA addendum that includes "no training on Aurora customer data" clause and a DocuSign envelope for signature.
3) Redwood infra: schedule opt-out gating on ingestion pipeline and verify audit logs export; target implementation in 2–3 business days after signed DPA.

If that matches, please reply with an explicit confirmation (we need a line from legal to attach to the contract) and we’ll route the DocuSign link.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity on this.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

Attachments: redwood_security_summary.pdf (pdf), aurora_data-retention-FAQ.docx (docx)

Subject: Re: Post-call: Aurora Health — Data use & training exclusions

Thanks, Rishi — this is helpful and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirming: Aurora requires that no customer-identifiable content or request/response pairs be used to train Redwood models. That includes any manual review for labeling.
- Retention: we prefer 90 days for request logging and 365 days for security audit logs. We understand some telemetry can be aggregated; any aggregated telemetry used for product quality must be irreversible and non-identifying.
- Residency: production inference and backups must remain within US data centers (us-east-1) for any environment that may contain PHI. Analytics exports for product improvement may be EU/US only after anonymization and Aurora approval.
- SOC2: please send the SOC 2 summary and the DPA addendum. Legal is cc’d (legal@aurorahealth.com) and will review the addendum and DocuSign.

I’ll ask Tom (cc) to confirm from procurement whether we need a PO as well; we might move quickly on the POC once the DPA is signed.

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Aurora Health — Data use & training exclusions (DPA & DocuSign)

Folks — following Elena's confirmation, attaching the DPA addendum that includes the explicit model-training exclusion clause and the DocuSign envelope link for signature. Please see the key language below and let me know if legal needs an alternate phrasing.

Key clause (summary)
- Redwood will NOT use Aurora customer content, request/response payloads, or any identifiers for model training, fine-tuning, or human labeling, unless Aurora provides explicit written consent.
- Redwood may collect aggregated, irreversible telemetry for product quality; such telemetry will exclude PII and cannot be reverse-engineered to identify customers.
- Audit logs and administrative traces will be retained per the agreed retention schedule (Aurora: 90 days for request logs; 365 days for security/audit logs).
- Data residency: customer data for Aurora production workloads will be stored and processed in us-east-1; backups flagged as PHI will not be moved outside the US.

Attachments included here: docusign_training-exclusion.pdf (DocuSign envelope, includes addendum), redwood_security_summary.pdf (SOC 2 high-level). DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/XYZ-987654

Timeline
- Once signed, we’ll apply the opt-out pipeline gating immediately (expect 24–72 hours for full enforcement across environments).

Thanks — looping in Dev so infra/legal can track the implementation.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: docusign_training-exclusion.pdf (pdf), redwood_security_summary.pdf (pdf)
